text:
maria_support: Customer (ACME) reported a 400 from our embeddings/rerank endpoint — error text: "embedding vector size mismatch". They attached a payload and a response header with request-id: r-0a1b2c3d4e. Can someone collect repro steps (curl), logs, and a debug bundle? Need quick triage and an ETA to customer.

eli_sde: can you paste the exact request headers + model name? suspect either the client sent wrong-shaped vectors (e.g. 768 vs 1536) or batching munged the shape. Also include the full response (headers + body) so we can grab X-Request-ID from the response.

maria_support: pasted minimal sanitized payload from customer below (they redacted PII):
```json
{
  "model": "redwood-embed-large",
  "inputs": [
    [0.12, 0.03, 0.98, /* ... truncated ... */],
    [0.11, 0.04, 0.99, /* ... truncated ... */]
  ],
  "batching": true
}
```
Response body: {"error":"embedding vector size mismatch: expected 1536, got 768"}
Response headers include: X-Request-ID: r-0a1b2c3d4e

sam_prodengineer: i'll try a local repro. quick curl template for the customer to run and for us to mirror:

```bash
curl -i -X POST "https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/embeddings" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-large","inputs":[[0.12,0.03,0.98,...],[0.11,0.04,0.99,...]]}'
```

sam_prodengineer: when you paste the full response, I can grep logs with the request-id. i'll run with their exact vectors (sanitized) to reproduce.

eli_sde: also check whether they used our rerank endpoint accidentally (which expects pairs) vs embeddings endpoint. Rerank expects inputs like: {"queries": [...], "candidates": [[...],[...]]} — shape mistakes lead to misleading mismatch errors.

devin_research: low-effort checks to ask customer: 1) model name exact string, 2) whether they call embeddings or rerank API, 3) whether they serialized floats as strings ("0.12"), 4) whether the client lib is applying chunking/batching on its side.

ashley_oncall: i'm on infra duty, will grep ingestion and model-serve logs for r-0a1b2c3d4e. if found, i'll pull the model variant and kernel selection info. give me 10m.

ci-bot: debug bundle created: s3://redwood-debug/1734567890/r-0a1b2c3d4e-debug.tar.gz (includes ingress logs, model metadata, kernel trace) :package:  <-- automated upload after request-id observed in ingest logs

eli_sde: nice. when you have the bundle, please include: model config (expected embedding dim), request payload as received by gateway, and any batching/reshape logs. If the gateway reports automatically reshaped arrays, include that trace.

sam_prodengineer: repro notes for the team: i ran the supplied vectors against redwood-embed-large locally and got the same 400. turned out the customer was using a client that concatenated two 768-sized embeddings into one long vector per entry (so server received nested lists of wrong length). fixing their client to send two separate inputs to the batch fixed it.

maria_support: awesome, can you produce a minimal failing curl (with sanitized numbers) we can send back to ACME showing both the broken payload and the corrected payload? i'll include the debug bundle link.

sam_prodengineer: yes — will paste both examples in a follow-up message and add a short note about how to detect this on their side (check each input length == model.dimension).

devin_research: small suggestion for backend: add a clearer error string that includes expected vs received dims and maybe an RFC link to our batching docs for clients to avoid confusion.

maria_support: assigning sam to own the repro + reply to customer with the debug bundle and corrected curl. ashley will confirm infra/logs archived. eli if you want to follow the postmortem for a possible doc update.

ashley_oncall: confirmed logs archived at s3://redwood-logs/ingest/2024-11-21/r-0a1b2c3d4e.log.gz. no auth or billing anomalies present.

maria_support: thanks everyone — i'll update the ticket with the repro curl, debug bundle link, and recommended client fix. closing loop with ACME now. :white_check_mark:
